 Gabe Hauari USA TODAY Nov. 11, 2026, 11:14 a.m. ET Hear this story Whipped cream sold at Costco warehouses in a dozen states across the Midwest and Southeast has been recalled, according to the warehouse retailer.
 Alamance Foods, the manufacturer of Kirkland-brand whipped cream sold at Costco, announced Nov. 7 a voluntary recall of Kirkland Signature Real Heavy Whipped Cream because one batch "may contain a small amount of a cleaning chemical."
 According to the company, members reported a chemical smell and taste, but "no serious adverse effects requiring medical care" have been reported. Alamance Foods is advising consumers who purchased the affected product to stop using it and return it to your local Costco for a full refund.
 Here's what to know about the affected product.
